overview: This Senate resolution designates November 22, 2025, as National Adoption Day and November 2025 as National Adoption Month. It notes that about 329,000 children were in U.S. foster care, roughly 70,000 of them with a goal of adoption, and that thousands of young people each year risk leaving foster care as adults without a permanent family. It states that every child should have a permanent and loving family and encourages Americans to consider adopting, in November and throughout the year. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on November 20, 2025. It is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
for: Supporters say the resolution raises awareness of the many children in foster care who are waiting for families and encourages more people to consider adoption.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or funding to speed up adoptions or support foster children.
